title: Best Cordless Hedge Trimmers UK
short: Cordless hedge trimmers compared by cutting power, blade length and battery life, from lightweight shrub clippers to heavy-duty conifer-busting models.
intro: A hedge trimmer's cutting power and battery life matter more than blade length alone, since a trimmer that jams on thick branches makes any job slower. This guide compares trimmers tested by Expert Reviews on real conifer, box, laurel and hornbeam hedges in their own garden.

products.name: UniversalHedgeCut 18-55
products.best_for: Medium to large gardens with a range of hedge types
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top pick, chewing through everything from lonicera to laurel and sticky woody conifer hedging with ease. It's heavier than budget trimmers but gives much more cutting power, using Bosch's Power For All battery shared across the wider ecosystem, charging in just over an hour for up to 80 minutes of use.
pros: Unbeatable stamina and performance
Handles large and untidy hedges with ease
Shares batteries across the Power For All ecosystem

products.name: Comfort Cut 50/18V
products.badge: Best for small to mid-sized gardens
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong performance with excellent ergonomics
products.key_spec: 50cm blade, 20mm max branch width, non-slip handles
products.summary: Well-balanced and solidly built, with grippy handles and good protection, which Expert Reviews called one of the most ergonomic trimmers tested. It pushed smoothly through lonicera, privet, conifer and hornbeam with genuine cutting power for a lightweight model, though it runs a little noisy at peak.
pros: Great performance and ease of use
Comfortable, low-vibration handling
Shares Power For All batteries with Flymo, Husqvarna and Bosch

products.name: 20V Electric Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.best_for: Casual gardeners with just a small hedge or two
products.key_spec: 51cm blade, 15mm max branch width, includes battery and charger
products.summary: A budget kit that includes trimmer, battery and charger for what other brands charge for a bare tool alone. Expert Reviews found enough power for most hedging types, easily handling lonicera and hornbeam, though heavyweight conifer or laurel can jam it up.
pros: Includes battery and charger in the price
Handles most hedging types well
Batteries interchangeable with other Terratek tools
cons: Struggles with heavyweight conifer or laurel

products.name: 18V EasiCut 450
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this feels lighter than its actual weight thanks to good balance and comfortable handles, zipping through leaves and smaller branches without fuss. It's manoeuvrable for shaping lonicera or privet, though it lacks the power for thicker conifer hedges and jams beyond its 16mm max width.
pros: Comfortable, easy handling
Great manoeuvrability for shaping hedges
Chunky triggers and good blade guard
cons: Lacks power for thicker conifer hedges
16mm cutting width is a hard limit

products.name: DUH751Z
products.best_for: Buyers with masses of thick conifer or woody hedging
products.key_spec: 75cm blade, 23.5mm max branch width, triple-edged teeth
products.summary: A serious alternative to petrol models, with a massive blade and triple-edged tooth design that Expert Reviews found trimmed a thick fir hedge in double-quick time without jamming. Over 90 minutes of runtime from Makita's 18V 5.0Ah battery, though at 4.5kg it's heavy work on the arms.
pros: Breaks up even the toughest hedges
Very long runtime (90+ minutes)
Comfortable rotating handle
cons: Overkill for smaller hedges and gardens

products.name: Aspire H50-P4A
products.badge: Best for short hedges and shrubs
products.best_for: Compact hedges and shrubs that need real cutting power
products.summary: A compact trimmer with a powerful motor and wider tooth gap that Expert Reviews found sliced through branches up to 23mm without resistance, surpassing expectations on overgrown lonicera and dense conifer. A removable leaf catcher is a smart touch, and batteries are shared across Husqvarna, Gardena, Flymo and Bosch.
pros: Formidable cutting power for its size
Compact and easy to handle
Removable leaf catcher
Shares batteries across Power 4 All ecosystem
cons: Not ideal for large gardens with extensive hedging

products.name: WG801E
products.best_for: Topiary shaping and sculpting smaller shrubs
products.key_spec: 10-20cm blade, 8mm max branch width, 3 interchangeable blades
products.summary: A pint-sized handheld trimmer that Expert Reviews found genuinely useful for reaching up high and clipping tops, with three blades for different topiary needs or cutting grasses. Its real skill is shaping and sculpting smaller shrubs and lightweight box or lonicera hedging, though it's not for larger hedges.
pros: Great for shaping and sculpting shrubs
Lightweight, easy to wield up high
Three interchangeable blades included

products.name: HGE 18-50
products.best_for: Buyers who want an all-round trimmer for tough, unruly hedges
products.key_spec: 50cm blade, 22mm max branch width, rotating handle
products.summary: A great all-rounder that Expert Reviews found handled larger, tougher and more unruly shrubs and hedges with ease, from beech to hornbeam to overgrown conifer. An ingenious lever lets you rotate the blade around the top handle to match your working angle, with nearly an hour of runtime from the larger battery.
pros: Trims just about everything with ease
Rotating blade for comfortable working angles
Strong stamina from the battery
cons: The odd very thick branch can still slow it down

products.name: GE-HC 18 Li T
products.best_for: Reaching the top of hedges 7ft and above without a ladder
products.key_spec: 40cm blade on 1.7m telescopic pole, pivoting head, swappable chainsaw attachment
products.summary: An extendable trimmer that Expert Reviews found let them reach the top of a 2-3m hedge without a ladder, with a pivoting head for side or top trimming. A clever party trick: the head swaps for a mini-chainsaw attachment, which worked superbly on an overgrown hornbeam hedge and for light tree pruning.
pros: Reaches tall hedges without a ladder
Pivoting head for side and top trimming
Swappable mini-chainsaw attachment
Shares Power X-Change batteries with other Einhell tools
cons: Can feel unwieldy on smaller hedges

guide.q: What blade length do I need?
guide.a: A shorter blade (40-50cm), like the Gardena or Husqvarna here, is easier to manoeuvre for shaping and smaller hedges. A longer blade (55cm+), like the Bosch or Makita, covers more hedge per pass, better suited to long runs of hedging in a larger garden.

guide.q: What maximum branch width should I look for?
guide.a: For soft, regularly-trimmed hedges like privet or lonicera, a modest 15-16mm capacity is usually enough. For tougher or more overgrown hedging like conifer or laurel, look for a trimmer rated to at least 20-23mm to avoid jamming, like the Bosch, Husqvarna or Kärcher here.

guide.q: Is a telescopic or pole hedge trimmer worth it?
guide.a: If you have tall hedges (around 7ft or higher), a telescopic model like the Einhell here lets you trim the top safely without a ladder. For hedges you can comfortably reach from the ground, a standard handheld trimmer is lighter and easier to control.

guide.q: Does sharing a battery system across tools matter?
guide.a: Many brands, including Bosch, Gardena, Flymo and Husqvarna, use shared battery platforms (Power For All or Power 4 All), so a battery bought for one tool works across the whole range. This is worth checking if you already own other cordless garden tools, since it can save buying a spare battery and charger.
